chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Catching the cashier stealing, with the African waiter Baccuse
summary: A cashier was caught stealing by a bright young African waiter who could calculate like a computer, and Butler took back the money.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: He sees all these people in there. They get over there and do this. And I caught one of them girls at the cash -- she was stealing money.

And I had a little African, little African boy, his name was Baccuse (PHONETIC), and he -- well, Africans and me, we get along, got along very well together. So he's a waiter, and he was a busy little fellow, he could do anything. So -- and he could count as fast -- with a slight bit of education this boy could calculate so fast, just exactly like a computer. And she was saying, no, no, you've got so and so all this time. And she had stolen half of the ribbon off the typewriter. He said, no, you see what's been torn off? Here's another thing you forgot to look at (inaudible) and caught the poor child stealing.
I've got a picture there, someone took the picture, and I'm looking at her, and he's doing that. So she said,

Yeah, and I'm looking. And so I says, well, darling, you stole but that's all right (inaudible). Because after she stole it, I want to get the money back. Look like nothing's happened, and get your money back, see what I mean?
